description: Sierra Wireless EM7455 / MC7455 / EM7565 and the Dell DW5811e (an EM7455): family base, never matched itself. Qualcomm QMI modules on qcserial + qmi_wwan: interface 0 DM/DIAG, 2 NMEA, 3 AT, 8 QMI (a second QMI on 10 for EM74xx/MC74xx; MBIM in the module's other USB configuration). ModemManager's Sierra plugin owns them. Radio over AT is the Sierra dialect: AT!SELRAT mode, AT!BAND band sets, AT!GSTATUS? / AT!LTEINFO? telemetry; writes need AT!ENTERCND with the module's password first. The QDL/boot identities (1199:907a for EM74xx, 1199:9090 for EM7565) are service mode, not a modem; 1199:9078 and 1199:907b are EM74xx modem compositions (the kernel's qcserial and qmi_wwan tables). No AT eUICC probing on Sierra (a CCHO probe hung the SIM on the EM9190)

hints.at_source: Sierra layout DM 0, NMEA 2, AT 3, QMI 8 (Linux 6.12 drivers/usb/serial/qcserial.c QCSERIAL_SWI); ModemManager 1.25.95 src/plugins/sierra/77-mm-sierra.rules marks interface 3 AT primary for 1199:9071, 9079, 9091

radio.source: Sierra AirPrime EM74xx/MC74xx AT command reference (!SELRAT, !BAND, !ENTERCND); another modem manager 3.5.5 Sierra Gobi LTE profile (AT!GSTATUS?, AT!LTEINFO?, AT!BAND, AT!SELRAT after AT!ENTERCND); no field report of ours
